subject: science
passage: African wild dogs, which live and hunt in close-knit packs in parts of southern and eastern ______ seem to decide when to set off on a hunt by sneezing. In a study of packs in Botswana, the more often the dogs sneezed during a gathering, the more likely the pack was to leave and hunt.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The clause "which live and hunt in close-knit packs in parts of southern and eastern Africa" is extra information about the dogs. It opens with a comma after "dogs," so it must close with a comma before the verb "seem."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the "which" clause runs straight into the main verb "seem."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "African wild dogs" from its verb "seem."
explanation.C: Correct. The closing comma matches the comma after "dogs" and sets off the "which" clause, so the subject connects to its verb "seem."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause, and the words before it are not one.
